answer: Because the tundra derivation is checked against the wharf nonce, the kernel audit keeps the accepted values and a reused text fails on the first character. That binds the text to one identity's challenge, so copying between 120 aliases produces 120 mismatches and forfeits the authoring cost with no payout. An answer must include the first 17 hex characters of the seed it was derived under, and a wrong or missing derivation is rejected at intake.
